basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 24.' and it opens 'Vers. 24. Quintam regi dabitis. Quinta pars, quae regibus persolvebatur, quinque sensuum'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 24. Quintam regi dabitis. Quinta pars, quae regibus persolvebatur, quinque sensuum custodiam designat, quae Christo consecranda est. Nam et in lege praecipitur omne primogenitum masculini sexus quinque siclis argenti debere redimi. (Exod. XIII, 15.) Quod vero quatuor partes permittebantur habere, hoc designat quod unusquisque in laicali conversatione, hoc est actuali, secundum suum propositum vel facultatem permittitur vivere.
